texts.preamble: Sh. Rajiv Kumar & Ors. vs . Food Safety Officer, on 14 February, 2020 In The Court Of Sh. Anil Antil, Additionalsessions Judge04, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi A. Cr No. 360/18, Sh. Rajiv Kumar & Ors. Vs. Food Safety Officer, B. Cr No. 362/18 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Agarwal & Ors. Vs. Food Safety Officer C. Cr No. 13/19 Sh. Gulshan Chadha Vs. Food Safety Officer D. Cr No. 361/18 Pradeep Kumar Agarwal & Ors. Vs. Food Safety Officer E. Cr No. 284/18 Sh. H.P.S. Khatri Vs. Food Safety Officer Date of Institution: 17.09.2018 (In Cr No. 13/19 : 04.01.2019) Date of Arguments: 14.02.2020 Date of Order : 14.02.2020
texts.facts: Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 06.04.2015, the Food Safety Officer visited the Karkardooma area wherein allegedly one Ram Chander was intercepted and was found having stored/meant "Royal Zafrani Zarda" for sale for human consumption. The sample was taken. Necessary procedure under Food Safety & Standards Act was thereafter followed. That on the completion of investigation, vide report dated 21.04.2015, it was found from the report of Food Analyist that the sample was unsafe because it contained tobacco and Nicotine which was prohibited under Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety & Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sale), Regulation 2011, and for misbranding to be in violation of regulations 2.2.2.3 of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011. A sanction accordingly was obtained from the commissioner Food Safety GNCT on 20.04.2016. 5. That the complaint was then filed in the court of ACMM for the offence under Section 26/52/59 of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006. Cognizance of the offences was taken by the learned ACMM and the accused persons were thereafter summoned to face the trial. The said order has been assailed by the revisionists in these revision petitions.
texts.arguments: 6. The main contention of the Revisionists is that the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006 is not applicable to the present case as `Zarda', which is Tobacco product, is not governed by the Food Adulteration Act but in fact it is governed by the Cigarettes and other Tobacco products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003. It is further submitted that 'Zarda' is a proprietary food and there is no standard for it under the Food Safety and Standard Act, Therefore it cannot apply to the sample commodity. In these circumstances, the Food Safety Officer has no right to collect the sample and to prosecute the revisionists under the provision of the FSS Act. 7. To buttress his arguments, learned counsel for the revisionists has relied upon the recent judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as 'Food Inspector vs. CR No. 360/18, 362/18, 13/19, 361/18 & 284/18 Page No. 2 of 3 Rupesh Jain & Ors. 2018(1) FAC 145, and other cases tilted as Ram Babu Rastogi and Ors. vs. State through Food Inspector (PFA)2012(1) FAC 56; S. Salem Babu and Anr. vs. The Food safety Inspector 2016(2) FAC 432 and Jayavllas Tobacco Traders LLP vs. The Designated Officer 2017)2) FAC 359. 8. During arguments , learned SPP for the Department fairly conceded to the law laid down by the authorities relied upon by the revisionists and also the fact that the said orders have thereafter not been assailed by the department before the superior court and thus attained finality.
